Let me analyze this OIML certificate for a water meter (Sappel type A1, R49/2006).

Key facts:
- Certificate number: R49/2006-FR2-10.04 rev.0
- Issuing authority: Laboratoire National de Métrologie et d'Essais (LNE), France
- Person responsible: Thomas LOMMATZSCH
- Signed by: Laurence DAGALLIER, Deputy Director
- Applicant: SAPPEL, 67 rue du Rhône, 68304 SAINT LOUIS CEDEX, FRANCE
- Manufacturer: SAPPEL, 67 rue du Rhône, 68304 SAINT LOUIS CEDEX, FRANCE
- Certified type: Water meter type A1 (Compteur d'eau type A1)
- Accuracy class: 2
- Recommendation: R49/2006
- Issued: October 13, 2010
- Pages: 5
- Member state: FRANCE

Test reports:
- Test report n°LB A1 003 - 30/07/2009, 270 pages
- Test report n°LB A1 002 - 29/11/2007, 200 pages
- Test report n°LB A1 001 - 25/03/2003, 146 pages
- Test report n°OIML AQU034 - 28/07/2005, 239 pages
- Test report n°OIML AQU034 - 01/06/2005, 170 pages
- Test report n°OIML AQU034 - 06/09/2004, 351 pages
- Test report n°OIML AQU034 - 25/03/2003, 146 pages

Now the annex tables: 4 tables (pages 2-5), each describing a variant family.

Table 1 (page 2): "Linear and concentric" version
- Register: Plastic / Plastic G1 / Glass / Glass G1
- Body: Brass
- Connections: Threads 5/8", 3/4", 7/8", 1", 1 1/4", 1 1/2"
- DN 15 and DN 20
- Q3: 2.5 (DN15), 4.0 (DN20)
- Q4: 3.125 (DN15), 5.0 (DN20)
- Q3/Q1: DN15: 40...400 (11 values); DN20: 40...500 (12 values)
- Q2/Q1: 1.6
- Position: all positions
- Length: 105; 110; 114; 115; 130; 134; 135; 145; 165; 170; 175; 180; 190; 191 mm
- Max pressure: 16 bar
- Water temp: 0.1–30 (T30) / 0.1–50 (T50)
- Indicator range: 9 999 / 99 999 m³
- Verification scale interval: 0.020 or 0.050 dm³
- Min upstream/downstream length: 0/0 mm
- Cycle volume: 55 cm³
- Accuracy class 2
- Mechanical environment: not applicable
- Climatic: +5°C; +55°C
- Electromagnetic: not applicable
- Environment class (OIML R49): not applicable
- Reverse flow: No

Table 2 (page 3): "Linear" version
- Same register/body
- Connections: 5/8" to 1 1/2"
- DN 15 and DN 20
- Q3: 2.5 (both)
- Q4: 3.125 (both)
- Q3/Q1: 80; 100; 125; 160; 200
- Q2/Q1: 1.6
- Temp: 0.1–90 (T90) / 30–90 (T30/90)
- Cycle volume: 55 cm³
- Rest same.

Table 3 (page 4): "Linear" version
- Connections: 1 1/4", 1 1/2", 2"
- DN 25
- Q3: 6.3, 6.3, 10 (three columns)
- Q4: 7.875, 7.875, 12.5
- Q3/Q1: col1: 160;200;250;315; col2: 40...315; col3: 40...500
- Lengths: col1: 260 mm; col2&3: 260; 300 mm
- Temp: 0.1–30 (T30) / 0.1–50 (T50)
- Cycle volume: col1: 81 cm³; col2&3: 314 cm³
- Rest same.

Table 4 (page 5): "Linear" version
- Connections: 1 1/4" to 2 1/2"
- DN 32 and DN 40
- Q3: 10 (DN32), 16 (DN40)
- Q4: 12.5 (DN32), 20 (DN40)
- Q3/Q1: DN32: 40...500 (12 values); DN40: 40...800 (14 values)
- Length: 260; 300 mm
- Temp: 0.1–30 (T30) / 0.1–50 (T50)
- Cycle volume: 314 cm³
- Rest same.

Now, how to structure this. The models are variants by DN (nominal diameter) and version (linear/concentric). Actually the axis of variation is: version (Linear and concentric vs Linear), DN (15, 20, 25, 32, 40), and Q3.

A reasonable model_family: models keyed by DN and version:

Table 1: DN15 (linear and concentric), Q3=2.5; DN20 (linear and concentric), Q3=4.0
Table 2: DN15 (linear), Q3=2.5; DN20 (linear), Q3=2.5
Table 3: DN25 (linear) with three sub-variants: Q3=6.3 (cycle vol 81, length 260, Q3/Q1 160-315), Q3=6.3 (cycle vol 314, length 260/300, Q3/Q1 40-315), Q3=10 (cycle vol 314, length 260/300, Q3/Q1 40-500)
Table 4: DN32 (linear), Q3=10; DN40 (linear), Q3=16

Model IDs could be like "A1-DN15-Q3=2.5" etc. But since some columns differ within DN 25, we need distinct model IDs.

Let me define models:
1. model_id "DN15-linear-concentric-Q3=2.5" — table 1 col 1
2. model_id "DN20-linear-concentric-Q3=4.0" — table 1 col 2
3. model_id "DN15-linear-Q3=2.5" — table 2 col 1
4. model_id "DN20-linear-Q3=2.5" — table 2 col 2
5. model_id "DN25-linear-Q3=6.3-cycle81" — table 3 col 1
6. model_id "DN25-linear-Q3=6.3-cycle314" — table 3 col 2
7. model_id "DN25-linear-Q3=10" — table 3 col 3
8. model_id "DN32-linear-Q3=10" — table 4 col 1
9. model_id "DN40-linear-Q3=16" — table 4 col 2

That's 9 variants. For Q3/Q1, these are lists of ratios (R values), so values could be represented as lists of numbers... The schema says "Lists of values" that represent model variants go to model_level; but here Q3/Q1 ratio is a selectable range (manufacturer picks one ratio from the list). Hmm. For water meters, Q3/Q1 is a designation ratio; the certificate approves a range of ratios. So value would be a list. The schema's value can be a number, {min,max}, or string. A list of values... Perhaps I should represent it as a string "40;50;..." or better as {min: 40, max: 500} range plus note. Actually the list is a set of allowed values, not necessarily contiguous R10 series... 40,50,63,80,100,125,160,200,250,315,400,500,630,800 — these are R10/R20 series values. I could represent as a string listing them, or as {min,max} with the note that they're the R-series. Hmm.

Given the schema strictness, I think using a string for the list is acceptable since value can be a string. But the guidance prefers numbers. For Q3/Q1, I could do {min: 40, max: 500} but that would falsely imply all intermediate values are allowed — although the listed values are essentially the whole R10 series between 40 and 500, so a range would be nearly accurate. Still, safer to keep as string list? The schema example shows ranges become {min,max}. For a set of discrete ratios, I'll keep the string form with semicolons — but rule 2 says numbers not strings for numbers. However, this is a list, and lists-as-values are discouraged ("emit model_matrix instead, NOT a list-as-value") — but here it's genuinely a set of approved options, not a family indicator.

Alternative: use config_level for Q3/Q1 with condition per model. Hmm, that's overcomplicating.

I think the cleanest: in model_level, attribute "q3_over_q1" with value being a string listing the allowed ratios, e.g. "40;50;63;80;100;125;160;200;250;315;400". Or value as {min: 40, max: 400}. I'll go with string lists to preserve fidelity, since these are discrete approvals. Actually wait — maybe better to normalize: use {min, max} and add attribute note? There's no notes field. I'll use string lists.

Hmm, but let me reconsider: maybe represent q3/q1 as a range is misleading. I'll keep string.

Similarly, "length" is a list of allowed lengths: 105..191 (14 values). Keep as string list.

Indicator range "9 999 / 99 999" — this is two options for the register range (5-digit or 6-digit). Value could be string "9999/99999" or a list. I'll use string "9999/99999".

Verification scale interval: 0.020 or 0.050 dm³ → string "0.020/0.050"? Or list. I'll use string "0.020 or 0.050"? Better: value as array? Schema doesn't allow arrays explicitly. Use string "0.020/0.050".

Water temperature range: "0,1 à 30" (T30) / "0,1 à 50" (T50) — two variants. Table 2 has T90: 0.1–90 and T30/90: 30–90. So this varies per table. I could encode as config_level with axis "temperature_class" (T30, T50, T90, T30/90), values: {condition: "T30", value: {min:0.1,max:30}}, etc. That fits config_level nicely: attribute water_temperature_range, axis oiml_r49_temperature_class, values [{condition:"T30", value:{min:0.1,max:30}, unit_symbol:"°C"}, ...]. But which temperature classes apply to which model? Tables 1,3,4 have T30/T50; table 2 has T90/T30-90. Mapping to specific models: DN15/20 linear-concentric: T30, T50; DN15/20 linear: T90, T30/90; DN25, DN32, DN40: T30, T50. Hmm, config_level conditions don't tie to models directly. Alternatively put per-model in model_level: attribute "water_temperature_range" with values per model being a list of ranges? Value could be a string like "0.1–30 (T30) / 0.1–50 (T50)". Hmm.

Simplest faithful approach: for each model, water_temperature_range value as a string listing the approved ranges with their class labels. But rule says numbers not strings... it's a pair of ranges though. I could emit model_level with two entries: for the temperature there are two sub-variants per model.

Alternative cleaner: use config_level with axis "temperature_class" and include the ranges:

config_level: [
  {
    "attribute": "water_temperature_range",
    "axis": "temperature_class",
    "values": [
      {"condition": "T30", "value": {"min": 0.1, "max": 30}, "unit_symbol": "°C"},
      {"condition": "T50", "value": {"min": 0.1, "max": 50}, "unit_symbol": "°C"},
      {"condition": "T90", "value": {"min": 0.1, "max": 90}, "unit_symbol": "°C"},
      {"condition": "T30/90", "value": {"min": 30, "max": 90}, "unit_symbol": "°C"}
    ]
  }
]

And then also indicate per model which classes apply? That's getting complex. Maybe I add a model_level attribute "temperature_classes" with value string "T30/T50" or "T90/T30-90" per model. That covers both.

Actually, I could put temperature_class_options per model in model_level, and the ranges in config_level. That's reasonable.

Matrix tables: The 4 annex tables are matrix tables. I'll emit matrix_tables[] with each table: name, columns, rows, description, footnotes. Columns like: version, register, body, connections, nominal_dn_mm, q3_m3h, q4_m3h, q3_q1, q2_q1, position, length_mm, map_bar, water_temp, indicator_range_m3, verification_scale_interval_dm3, min_upstream_downstream_length_mm, cycle_volume_cm3, accuracy_class, etc. But the tables have header-column structure where first cell is the attribute and subsequent columns are DN variants. Rows as objects per attribute might be more faithful: rows keyed by attribute with values per column. The schema says "rows[] (object per row)". In the R137 example, rows are per size (model) with attributes as keys. Here the table is transposed: rows are attributes, columns are variants. I can still emit rows as objects: {"attribute": "nominal_dn", "DN15": 15, "DN20": 20}? That's awkward. 

Better: convert to per-variant rows, like the R137 example: each row is a variant with columns q3, q4, q3_q1, dn. And shared attributes go in description or as columns with same values. Let me build matrix_tables with rows per column-variant:

Table 1 "Linear and concentric version (DN15, DN20)":
columns: ["nominal_dn_mm", "q3_m3_h", "q4_m3_h", "q3_q1", "cycle_volume_cm3"] — plus length? Length is shared for all: 105-191 list. Could be a column with same value, or description.

Hmm, but table 3 has 3 sub-columns with varying length and cycle volume. Let me make columns: ["variant", "dn_mm", "q3_m3_h", "q4_m3_h", "q3_over_q1_options", "length_mm", "cycle_volume_cm3", "water_temperature_classes", "connections"]. rows per variant.

Actually to preserve fidelity and also feed model_level, I'll do both: matrix_tables entries mirroring each annex page, and model_level characteristics.

Given the effort, let me now define canonical model IDs. Perhaps: "DN15 (linear and concentric), Q3=2.5" etc. Keep model_id concise: "DN15-LC-Q3=2.5"? Use readable: "A1 DN15 linear and concentric Q3=2.5". Hmm, model_id should be a compact identifier. I'll use:

- "DN15-linear-concentric-Q3=2.5"
- "DN20-linear-concentric-Q3=4.0"
- "DN15-linear-Q3=2.5"
- "DN20-linear-Q3=2.5"
- "DN25-linear-Q3=6.3-V1" (cycle 81, length 260)
- "DN25-linear-Q3=6.3-V2" (cycle 314)
- "DN25-linear-Q3=10"
- "DN32-linear-Q3=10"
- "DN40-linear-Q3=16"

Labels: descriptive.

Now type_level characteristics (common to all):
- accuracy_class: 2 (dimensionless)
- version... no, varies.
- register: string "Plastic / Plastic G1 / Glass / Glass G1" — this is a component option list; keep as type_level string.
- body: "Brass"
- q2_over_q1: 1.6
- position: "all positions"
- connections: varies by table → model_level? Table 1&2: 5/8"–1 1/2"; table 3: 1 1/4", 1 1/2", 2"; table 4: 1 1/4"–2 1/2". So connections vary → model_level.
- map (maximum admissible pressure): 16 bar
- indicator_range: "9999/99999" m³
- verification_scale_interval: "0.020/0.050" dm³
- min_upstream_downstream_pipe_length: {min:0,max:0} mm → value 0 mm.
- mechanical_environment_class: "Not applicable"
- climatic_environment_class: {min:5, max:55} °C
- electromagnetic_environment_class: "Not applicable"
- environment_class_r49: "Not applicable"
- reverse_flow_measurement: false / "No"

model_level characteristics:
- nominal_diameter_dn (mm) per model
- q3_permanent_flowrate (m³/h) per model
- q4_overload_flowrate (m³/h) per model
- q3_over_q1_options (string list) per model
- length (mm) per model (list string)
- connections per model (string)
- cycle_volume (cm³) per model
- water_temperature options per model: I'll do two attributes? "water_temperature_range" with value string like "0.1–30 (T30); 0.1–50 (T50)"? Or emit temperature ranges via config_level. Let me do:
  - model_level attribute "temperature_class" value string "T30/T50" or "T90/T30-90"? Actually the annex gives water temp range with the R49 class designation in parentheses. So per model: attribute "water_temperature_ranges" value string "0.1–30 (T30) / 0.1–50 (T50)". Hmm, but numbers-as-strings rule... It's a compound. I think acceptable as string since it's a set of ranges with labels. Alternatively config_level as planned plus model_level "temperature_classes" listing "T30, T50". I'll do:
  - model_level: attribute "temperature_classes", values per model: ["T30","T50"] as string "T30; T50".
  - config_level: attribute "water_temperature_range", axis "OIML R49 temperature class", values T30 {0.1,30}, T50 {0.1,50}, T90 {0.1,90}, T30/90 {30,90}.

That's clean.

Now version attribute per model: "Linear and concentric" vs "Linear". Add model_level "version".

Let me now build matrix_tables. I'll create 4 matrix tables corresponding to the 4 annex pages, with columns and rows per variant:

Table A: name "Linear and concentric version (DN15, DN20)"
columns: ["nominal_dn_mm", "q3_m3_h", "q4_m3_h", "q3_q1_options", "length_options_mm", "cycle_volume_cm3", "water_temperature_classes"]
rows:
- {"nominal_dn_mm": 15, "q3_m3_h": 2.5, "q4_m3_h": 3.125, "q3_q1_options": "40;50;63;80;100;125;160;200;250;315;400", "length_options_mm": "105;110;114;115;130;134;135;145;165;170;175;180;190;191", "cycle_volume_cm3": 55, "water_temperature_classes": "T30; T50"}
- {"nominal_dn_mm": 20, "q3_m3_h": 4.0, "q4_m3_h": 5.0, "q3_q1_options": "40;50;63;80;100;125;160;200;250;315;400;500", ...}

Hmm wait — in table 1, does the cycle volume differ between DN15 and DN20? "Volume cyclique (cm³) 55" colspan 2 → both 55. Yes.

Common attributes (register, body, position, pressure, indicator range, V, lengths upstream/downstream, accuracy class, environment classes, reverse flow) can go in "description" for each matrix table. Or I could include them as columns with constant values. The R137 example includes all columns including constant ones. But that bloats. I'll include key varying columns plus put shared attributes in description text.

Actually, let me reconsider: maybe simpler and more faithful to have matrix_tables rows keyed by attribute (transposed), i.e. rows: [{attribute: "Version", value: "Linear and concentric"}, ...]. The schema example shows rows keyed by size with attribute columns. I'll follow the R137 pattern (per-variant rows) since that's what's exemplified.

Table B: "Linear version (DN15, DN20)":
- DN15: Q3 2.5, Q4 3.125, Q3/Q1: 80–200 (80;100;125;160;200), length list same, cycle 55, temp T90/T30-90
- DN20: same Q3 2.5, Q4 3.125, same Q3/Q1, temp T90/T30-90

Table C: "Linear version (DN25)":
- col1: Q3 6.3, Q4 7.875, Q3/Q1: 160;200;250;315, length 260, cycle 81
- col2: Q3 6.3, Q4 7.875, Q3/Q1: 40–315 list, length 260;300, cycle 314
- col3: Q3 10, Q4 12.5, Q3/Q1: 40–500 list, length 260;300, cycle 314

Table D: "Linear version (DN32, DN40)":
- DN32: Q3 10, Q4 12.5, Q3/Q1 40–500, length 260;300, cycle 314
- DN40: Q3 16, Q4 20, Q3/Q1 40–800, length 260;300, cycle 314

Connections per table:
- Table A & B: threads 5/8", 3/4", 7/8", 1", 1 1/4", 1 1/2"
- Table C: threads 1 1/4", 1 1/2", 2"
- Table D: threads 1 1/4", 1 1/2", 2", 2 1/2"

Now certificate-level fields:
- number: "R49/2006-FR2-10.04" with revision 0. The schema has revision_history. Number: "R49/2006-FR2-10.04". Hmm, but the certificate number includes rev.0 typically. I'll put number "R49/2006-FR2-10.04" and revision_history [{"revision": "0", ...}] — but revision date? Revision 0 is initial issue on 2010-10-13. The rev number appears as "rev.0" in the cert number. I'll include revision_history with revision "0", date "2010-10-13", changes "Initial issue".
- scheme: "A" — OIML-CS scheme A is the classic certificate of conformity without separate modules. These 2010 LNE certs are scheme A. Yes, scheme "A".
- project_number: not present. There's "CIM6-V4-01-2010" which is a form reference (LNE internal form), and "Référence LNE-19888 rév. n° 0" — document reference of the form. Not a project number. Omit project_number. Actually "720 CIM 0701-56 rev0 du 24/04/2008" is the annex form reference. Omit.
- page_total: 5 (appendix consists of 5 pages). The certificate says "comprend 5 page(s)". The whole document: 1 main + 5 annex = 6. The "page_total" probably refers to certificate pages; the annex has 5 pages. I'll use 5? Hmm. "page_total" — document-level field. The main certificate page says the appendix "consists of 5 page(s)". The page footers show "Page 1 / 5" ... "Page 5 / 5". I'll set page_total: 5.
- member_state: "FRANCE"
- date_issued: "2010-10-13"
- oiml_issuer_id: not given explicitly. There's COFRAC accreditation n° 5-0012. Omit oiml_issuer_id.

issuing_authority:
- name: "Laboratoire National de Métrologie et d'Essais"
- address_lines: ["1, rue Gaston Boissier", "75724 Paris Cedex 15"]
- person_responsible: "Thomas LOMMATZSCH" (person responsible). Also Laurence DAGALLIER signed as deputy director. The schema has person_responsible and person_title. Thomas LOMMATZSCH is "Personne responsable". The signature block: "Laurence DAGALLIER, Délégataire / Directrice Déléguée / Deputy Director" signing for the Director General. I'll set person_responsible: "Laurence DAGALLIER"? Hmm. The cert explicitly labels Thomas LOMMATZSCH as "Person responsible". The signer is Laurence DAGALLIER. I'll use person_responsible: "Thomas LOMMATZSCH" and... maybe add the signer? Schema doesn't have signer field. I could use person_responsible: "Thomas LOMMATZSCH", person_title: null. Or include Laurence DAGALLIER with title "Deputy Director" as person_responsible since she signed on behalf. The label "Person responsible" in the cert is attached to Thomas LOMMATZSCH. I'll go with Thomas LOMMATZSCH. Hmm, but the signing authority is DAGALLIER. The schema is limited; choose the explicit "person responsible". 

Actually, wait — maybe I can note both: person_responsible "Thomas LOMMATZSCH", person_title null. Fine.

- phone: "01 40 43 37 00" → "+33 1 40 43 37 00"? Keep as given: "01 40 43 37 00".
- email: "info@lne.fr"
- website: "www.lne.fr"
- oiml_issuer_id: omit.

applicants: [{name: "SAPPEL", address_lines: ["67 rue du Rhône", "68304 SAINT LOUIS CEDEX", "FRANCE"]}]
manufacturers: same.

certified_type:
- category: "Water meter"
- type_designations: ["A1"]
- module_designation: null / omit (or "Not applicable"? For water meters there's no module concept like load cells; omit).
- description: "Water meter type A1" — maybe more: version linear / linear and concentric, register plastic/glass, body brass. Could write a description: "Water meter type A1, linear and linear-and-concentric versions, brass body, plastic or glass register, DN 15 to DN 40, Q3 from 2.5 to 16 m³/h." That's derived info; acceptable as free-text description? Rule 8: don't fabricate. Derived summary is fine but keep minimal: "Water meter type A1 (compteur d'eau)". I'll write "Water meter type A1".

recommendation: id "R49", edition 2006. The recommendation is "R49/2006" → id "R49", edition: 2006. accuracy_classes: [2] — R49 water meter accuracy class 2. Yes.
